_readme: Machine-readable catalog of the marketing component library (the Lovable design-system.json idea). The PreToolUse marketing-guard injects a digest of this file into every write/edit under app/[locale]/(marketing)/** or components/marketing/**, so the full expressive range is in context on every generation — not just the archetypes the model happens to remember. Keep entries in sync when a component's props change; guard lines render as `Name(props) — use`.
contract: Every content block sits in <Section>/<Container>/<SectionHeader> — spacing/width come from marketing tokens, never per-page values
Tokens only: hsl(var(--token)) / token Tailwind classes; must look right in the active palette × light/dark
Headings: font-display text-display-{2xl,xl,lg,md} (fluid clamp scale, no breakpoint font jumps). Urbanist: font-extrabold on the display scale, font-bold on any heading below it
Copy through the marketing i18n namespace (pt-BR, ONE's one language); no hardcoded strings
Icons only via @/icons/nexture/ni-* alias; meaningful concept icons, never decoration
Exactly one <h1> per page (Hero, or SectionHeader/PricingSection as/headingAs="h1")

New public pages: folder under app/[locale]/(marketing) named after the Portuguese path + declared in src/i18n/routing.ts + src/app/sitemap.ts when indexed + generateMetadata spreading publicPageMetadata (lib/seo.ts)
Internal links through <LocaleLink> (also as MUI LinkComponent) with the Portuguese path: it renders the address of the language being read; /auth/* and external URLs pass through
Structured data via <JsonLd> only; Organization/FAQPage/Product already emitted by layout/Faq/PricingSection

Motion is CSS first: the hero entrance (built into <Hero>), <Float>, <Reveal> (a transition started by watchEntry in motion.ts), <CountUp>; transform + opacity; reduced-motion safe. No scripted timeline, no ScrollTrigger: GSAP is loaded by <Parallax> alone, on demand
Layer scale: compositions are relative isolate with z-0 (back) / z-10 (frame) / z-20 (front); z-30 is reserved for site chrome

Ambient motion is seasoning and it ends: max 4 <Float> + 2 <Parallax> per page, always reduced-motion safe; one orbiting decor at most; never an animation that runs forever (an idle page must do no work)

tones.rule: primary is reserved for CTAs and the page's one bold moment; categorical elements (plan tiers, feature families, chart series, icon chips) take accent hues with a CONSISTENT family→hue mapping across the whole site. A 100%-primary page reads monochrome and fails the premium bar.

components.name: Section
components.props: spacing: default|compact, background: default|paper|primary-soft|contrast|deep, decor: none|glow|grid|gradient-edge|dots|mesh|orbit, bleed, id
components.use: vertical rhythm unit wrapping every block; vary background/decor at least twice along a page (premium bar #3); orbit is the one slowly-alive ambient — max one per page; deep = the dark band (--background-deep + text-text-contrast, a neutral that stays dark under any palette), never pair with light decors; always clips horizontal overflow (overflow-x-clip, not hidden: sticky columns keep working), so a frame glow or the orbit ring never widens the page at 375px

components.name: ProductComposition
components.props: frame (ProductFrame/screenshot), satellites: {children, position: top-left|top-right|right|bottom-right|bottom-left|left, depth: front|back, rotate: -6..6, float, floatDelay, parallax, hideBelow}[] (2–4)
components.use: LAYERED hero media — central frame + floating chips overlapping its edges (the reference-site look); collapses to a chip row below md; the hero entrance (CSS) choreographs the frame and then the satellites (premium bar #9); the composition gives each satellite its shadow on the layer that floats with it (a shadow left on the still wrapper showed as a second edge under a floating chip)

components.name: SatelliteChips
components.props: KpiChip{label,value,delta?,tone} · TrendChip{label,data?,tone} · AvatarRowChip{names,label} · ReadoutChip{text,tone} · RingChip{label,total,parts:{label,value,tone}[]}
components.use: ready-made satellites for ProductComposition; REAL localized content only — a satellite that lies is worse than none; the hue rides on the pill, the dot or the ring and the words keep text colours (a hue as small text over its own tint fails 4.5:1); RingChip is a donut of 2–4 parts with its total in the centre and a dot legend

components.name: ProductShot
components.props: name (basename under /images/marketing), alt (translated), sizes, priority (above the fold only), width?, height?
components.use: REAL product screenshot pair (light + -dark) captured by npm run shots:marketing; use inside ProductFrame/Breakout media — real imagery beats any placeholder (premium bar #12)

components.name: Band
components.props: angle: -2..2, background: contrast|primary-soft|paper, spacing: default|compact|tight (half the compact space, for a one-line strip), decor: none|grid|dots, id, track
components.use: full-bleed ANGLED contrast strip — the diagonal-band breakout; background skews, content stays level; use INSTEAD of <Section> for that block (premium bar #10)

components.name: Breakout
components.props: side: right|left, media, children (copy column)
components.use: media escaping the container to the viewport edge; use inside <Section bleed className="overflow-x-clip">; copy column stays aligned with the site container (premium bar #10)

components.name: Float
components.props: amplitude?, duration?, delay?, rotate?, className
components.use: gentle oscillation for satellites/decor: a CSS animation on the compositor that settles after five cycles (an endless one keeps the main thread ticking while any IntersectionObserver is alive); reduced-motion static; budget ≤ 4 per page; no script, usable from server components

components.name: Parallax
components.props: speed (yPercent, capped 12), className
components.use: scroll-scrubbed drift for layered media; desktop-only + reduced-motion safe; budget ≤ 2 per page; the only component that loads GSAP (and ScrollTrigger), on demand, so a page without it downloads neither

components.name: CountUp
components.props: value (pre-formatted string), duration?, className
components.use: numbers count up when they enter the viewport (a short frame loop, started by watchEntry); SSR renders the final string (SEO/no-JS/reduced-motion correct); StatBand uses it internally

components.name: InView
components.props: threshold?, className
components.use: one-shot data-inview attribute on viewport entry — the CSS hook for server-rendered draw-ins (DataVizPlaceholder uses it internally)

components.name: Container
components.props: className
components.use: token width clamp; Section renders it — direct use only with Section bleed

components.name: SectionHeader
components.props: eyebrow, title, subtitle, align: start|center, as: h1|h2
components.use: standard section heading; as="h1" on the first header of hero-less pages

components.name: Hero
components.props: layout: center|split, decor: glow|grid|none, media (evidence slot), eyebrow, title (string or rich node — t.rich with <em> renders the two-tone headline), subtitle, primaryCta (unless action), secondaryCta{label, href, icon?}, action? (replaces the buttons with the conversion itself, e.g. the waitlist form), note?, highlights?: string[] (reassurance chips row, split only), strip?: {label, items: string[]} (center layout only: a labelled row of names under the note, e.g. the AIs the apps run on)
components.use: owns the page <h1> AND the page's one orchestrated motion moment: the entrance is CSS keyed on data-hero (style/layout/marketing-motion.css), copy line by line, then the media, then the satellites of a composition, starting with the first paint; a server component (no script of its own); split + <ProductFrame glow> is the committed direction for product-heavy pages; media is required in practice (premium bar #1)

components.name: ProductFrame
components.props: glow, children (real screenshot via next/image)
components.use: browser chrome for REAL product screenshots; token wireframe placeholder without children; glow = primary halo, the expensive-product hero treatment

components.name: PhoneFrame
components.props: time? (the status bar's clock), className, children (the screen)
components.use: a phone's chrome (status bar with the clock, the island, signal and battery) around a drawn screen, the frame of a ProductComposition when the evidence is what a client sees on their phone; its bezel is the deep band, so it reads as a phone under any palette

components.name: CaseMedia
components.props: ClientChat{firm, status, messages: {from: firm|client, text, time, link?}[], inputLabel} · ClientLinkPanel{firm, label, value, caption, documentsLabel, documents: {icon, label}[]} · CaseStageChart{title, total, stages: {label, value}[], highlight?}
components.use: ONE's product evidence drawn with tokens until its screens can be captured: a client's conversation on the firm's WhatsApp, answered by ONE (inside PhoneFrame), the client's link with the papers it gathered (a feature row's grey panel), the firm's cases by stage (a container: columns when the card is wide, a row per stage when it is narrow); every word from the marketing namespace, invented people only, and the page says the data is an example in a caption

components.name: DataVizPlaceholder
components.props: label
components.use: animated token-driven chart standing in for the screenshot on DATA products; CSS draw-in, reduced-motion safe

components.name: FeatureRows
components.props: items: {eyebrow?, title, body, bullets?, media, caption? (a line under the media: whose data it is), tone, cta?: {label, href, variant: primary|secondary}}, start: copy|media (which side the first row puts on the left at md+), decor, id, track, children? (what closes the same chapter, one row gap under the rows)
components.use: alternating text↔evidence zig-zag for the 2–4 flagship features; use INSTEAD of a second card grid; decor="grid" makes it the page's technical section; the eyebrow is text-coloured with a hue bar (no palette hue passes as small text on a light ground); a row's cta is the page's primary action repeated or its secondary (pastel) one; a drawn screen carries caption="Telas com dados de exemplo"

components.name: BentoGrid
components.props: items: {title, body, visual?, featured?, tone} — 4–7 cells
components.use: asymmetric grid; featured cells span 2 columns and carry a visual; breaks equal-card monotony; the seven trails of the home fill three rows (two featured)

components.name: StatBand
components.props: stats: {value (pre-formatted), label, tone} — 3–4 stats
components.use: contrast+grid band of OVERSIZED numbers (display-2xl, mono index, tone gauge bar) that COUNT UP on entry; doubles as a background break; invented stats are worse than none

components.name: ProcessSteps
components.props: steps: {icon?, kicker?, title, body, deliverableLabel?, deliverableValue?, tone}, variant: icon|mono
components.use: scannable sequence: ghosted ordinal + meaningful themed icon + optional deliverable, one hue per step; variant="mono" swaps to a mono 0N · kicker label (instrument treatment); in mono the hue rides on a bar above the label and the kicker keeps the text colour

components.name: FeatureGrid
components.props: features: {icon, title, description, tone}, variant: card|tinted, id, track
components.use: benefit-led card grid, meaningful icon per family hue; never the only archetype on a page (premium bar #2); variant="tinted" is a borderless wash of each family hue with the icon in a paper circle beside the title (the home's blueprint); three or six cards stand three abreast from md and stack below it

components.name: LogoCloud
components.props: label, items: {name, logo?}, band? (the strip on a full-bleed contrast Band tilted a degree: the page's breakout), track
components.use: trust strip; muted wordmarks until real token-tinted SVG logos exist; never a client who is not one (ONE's home lists the court systems it works with, and its label says so)

components.name: PricingSection
components.props: plans (from getDisplayPlans()), ctaLabel, ctaHref, headingAs: h1|h2, decor, id, tiers?: string[] (automation ladder above the grid), footnote? (differentiation line under it)
components.use: real plans, one highlighted anchor, tone per tier; emits Product JsonLd; CTA repeats the page's primary action verbatim; decor="glow" when it leads the page; 1–2 plans auto-center instead of stranding in a 3-up grid

components.name: Faq
components.props: eyebrow?, title, subtitle?, items: {question, answer, id?}, id?, track?, layout: stack|split (sticky intro + list)|aside (centred heading, the list beside a card for who did not find their question), link?: {label, href} (split), aside?: {title, body, cta: {label, href}} (aside)
components.use: REAL purchase objections (price, lock-in, security, updates) answered plainly; emits FAQPage JsonLd

components.name: Cta
components.props: title, subtitle, cta, secondaryCta? (deep and deep-panel: a second action; panel: a text link beside the button), points?: string[] (deep only), kicker?, decor: none|orbit|mesh|dots, variant: panel|deep|deep-panel
components.use: last conversion opportunity as a bordered console panel with primary glow + optional mono kicker; repeats the primary CTA verbatim; decor="orbit" is the classic closer; variant="deep-panel" is the deep band in a rounded panel with rays from the bottom left and a glow of the primary at the top right (the home's blueprint)

components.name: Reveal
components.props: stagger, delay, className
components.use: the ONLY sanctioned scroll animation: a CSS transition (transform + opacity) that plays once when the block reaches 85% of the viewport height; a block already on screen when the page hydrates is left alone (hiding it would make visible content blink); reduced-motion static; do NOT wrap every section uniformly — one orchestrated moment per page, the hero entrance (premium bar #5)

components.name: JsonLd
components.props: data (schema.org object)
components.use: the only way to emit structured data; never hand-write an ld+json <script>

components.name: Prose
components.props: className, children
components.use: long-form reading rhythm (legal pages, articles) without styling each element by hand

components.name: NumberStrip
components.props: items: {title, body}[] (3-4)
components.use: compact contrast band of numbered reassurance items under camel display ordinals (blueprint trust strip); sits right under the hero

components.name: Comparison
components.props: before/after: {label, title, items[]}
components.use: before/with-product cards joined by a bridge arrow — muted paper card vs deep teal card with camel checks; no blame language

components.name: RuledGrid
components.props: items: {icon?, title, body, tone?, link?: {label, href}, badge?, meta?}[], columns: 2|3|4, variant: light|deep|cards; RuledCard (named export) is one card of the cards variant, for grids that arrange cards themselves (StoreGrid)
components.use: hairline-ruled cell grid (benefits 3-col light, security 2-col deep) or separated cards (the module cards of /catalogo: badge beside the icon, a mono meta line for the version and AIs, a trailing link); meaningful concept icons in the family hue; the hue stays on the icon and the arrow, never on the words

components.name: IndexGrid
components.props: items: string[], accentEvery?: number
components.use: indexed hairline grid of categories (e.g. the seven catalog trails) with periodic deep accent cells; secondary-tone ordinals

components.name: LocaleLink
components.props: href (internal Portuguese path, query and hash kept), every next/link prop
components.use: every internal link of a public surface, and LinkComponent of MUI Buttons; never next/link directly on a public page, which would send an English reader to the Portuguese address

components.name: LegalDocument
components.props: slug: terms|privacy|cookies, path (internal Portuguese path), fallbackTitleKey, breadcrumbKey
components.use: a legal page: renders the consent term in force (consent_terms) in the language of the address, with version and date; an honest unavailable state, never a second copy of the terms in the catalogs
